sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Every reverse-outline summary written without the spec matches the controlling idea of its aligned spec paragraph (p01-p43), in spec order; the four opening callouts are not spec paragraphs and are matched to null.

The outliner marked only the KEY POINTS callout as holding two ideas; that callout is not a paragraph and the spec places all three thesis bullets in it by design. Every paragraph unit holds one idea.

Each unit traces to a supporting claim: opening scene and failure patterns to I1, argument to I2, who and why-exists to I3/I1, how-written and living journal to I4, organization, routing table, Veldmark and toolkit to I5/I4, conclusion synthesizes I1-I5.
The chart is followed by the competitor comparison and 'Why?', which frames the question as about matches.
The four green reports are followed by 'Nobody owns the question, because the question is not about any one of those systems.'
The four leaks are followed by 'The general manager's question is an architecture question' and what its answer runs through; Figure 1's caption says what it shows.
Each reader in the list is described by the boundary or stage they own.
The four parties' wants are followed by what the marketplace provides: the probability that the two sides find each other.
Amsterdam bikes vs rural Portuguese furniture is explained as liquidity measured per cell.
Figure 2 is explained by the claim that listings, search, trust and monetization are stages of one pipeline, and by its caption.
Each of the four examples says which liquidity it protects or spends.
The index-as-system-of-record and truncated-feed examples are presented as what engine documentation does not say.
The portfolio history is followed by 'The failures appear at the boundaries' and who can see them.
The five-kinds table says how to recognize each kind; Figure 3's caption restates that they are kept apart so each can be weighed.
Each example is named as the confusion it illustrates.
The two Adevinta quotations are followed by 'Both statements were true when they were written' and the consequence of citing without dates.
The three kinds of material are introduced as all a statement rests on, and the domain models are said not to be facts about real companies.
The parts table is introduced by the layout sentence and unpacked part by part in ¶2-¶10; Figure 4's caption says how the parts relate to the machine.
The routing table is preceded by how to use its columns and followed by the explanation of its two unexpected rows.

results.quote: **Five kinds of statement.** Architecture writing becomes unreliable when facts, habits, guesses, opinions and examples blur into one confident voice.
results.finding: Declared elaboration in a sentence carrying over 'real companies as precedents'; the opening picks up nothing from the company-aware paragraph and starts a new topic.

results.quote: The book opens with three preface pages, continues with eight parts that form a learning path along the machine
results.finding: Declared sequence sentence carrying over what the book's statements rest on; the section opens with the layout and does not pick up the preceding material (which ends on Veldmark filling gaps).
Declared sequence sentence carrying over the failure patterns, illustrated in every chapter; the section opens cold, with no link from the patterns to the group the illustrations come from.

results.quote: This book is a living journal, and a work in progress, that I revise as I learn more
results.finding: Declared sequence sentence carrying over the running example and the reference pages; the opening introduces how the book is kept current but picks up nothing from Veldmark, the toolkit or the glossary.

results.quote: draws it together: it maps each part to the stage of the machine it designs, the guarantee that stage must give, the liquidity metric it protects and the failure pattern that appears when it does not, and turns that map into marketplace fitness functions a group can measure every quarter
results.finding: Both readers re-read this sentence: 'it' has shifting referents (chapter, argument, part, stage) and 'marketplace fitness functions' is unexplained. The spec's order is fine; the sentence obscures it.
results.corroborated_by: flowA A1 and flowB B2 (same sentence: pronoun referents and the unexplained 'marketplace fitness functions')

results.quote: The book started from two generic domain models of marketplace businesses from my sibling repository
results.finding: Both readers could not place 'my sibling repository' (and the unexplained Productscape in Sources); the role of the domain models is unclear.
results.corroborated_by: flowA A3 and flowB B4 (same sentence: 'my sibling repository' cannot be placed)

results.quote: **What the five kinds of statement rest on.** Whatever its kind, every statement in the book rests on three kinds of material, and no other.
results.finding: After two paragraphs on dates and the as-of date, the section returns to the five kinds; B had to go back up to reconnect it to the table, A found it reads like an appendix, and both propose the same reorder (material and no-internal-material right after the five kinds and the three confusions, dates last). The difficulty comes from the spec's declared paragraph order within how-written (p20-p21 before p22-p23), not from the prose.
results.corroborated_by: flowB B3 and flowA section 2 ('How This Book Is Written': the 'what it rests on' paragraph 'comes after the dating discussion and reads a little like an appendix') with flowA section 4 proposing the same reorder as flowB section 4

results.quote: Whichever route you take into a chapter of Parts I to VIII, its opening callouts name the failure patterns it works on.
results.finding: Both readers stumbled on this opening and both marked the section's position only 'partly clear': after the routing table it steps back from 'go to your chapter' to previewing the next page, and nothing says why it comes here (the spec's reason: it and Veldmark are the subjects of the next two preface pages). 'its' first reads as pointing to 'route'. The spec's order is defensible; the prose does not state its reason.
results.corroborated_by: flowA A6 and flowB B6 (same sentence; both also mark The Failure Patterns 'partly clear' in section 2)

results.quote: Good material exists on each side of them.
results.finding: Reader A re-read: 'them' and 'on each side of' the stages are hard to picture until the next paragraph. Single reader.

results.quote: Whatever its kind, every statement in the book rests on three kinds of material, and no other.
results.finding: Reader A paused on 'kinds of statement' vs 'kinds of material', and noted that Veldmark illustrations rest on a fictional record, not on any of the three materials, which seems at odds with 'every statement ... and no other'. Single reader.

results.quote: which at Veldmark falls on Sunday evening
results.finding: Reader A found a Veldmark detail inside the parts overview out of place; reader B said it did not confuse. Single reader.

results.quote: The parts, the routing table, the failure patterns and Veldmark all turn it into a question you can ask of any design
results.finding: Reader A re-read the closing: 'it' changes referent within three sentences and the claim is abstract. Single reader.

results.quote: continues with eight parts that form a learning path along the machine, tests the patterns against public cases in Part IX
results.finding: Reader A had to check the count against 'nine parts' in the callouts; reader B reconciled it. Single reader.

results.quote: theirs against the team's estimate for a younger competitor
results.finding: Reader B could not tell which team made the estimate; 'Every team in the room' in the next paragraph means the system teams. Single reader.

results.quote: turns that map into marketplace fitness functions a group can measure every quarter
results.finding: 'marketplace fitness functions' is used without explanation or a promise of definition; it is not in the audience's already_knows. Other does_not_know terms (liquidity, learning to rank, percolation, DSA, VINs) are named only with an explicit promise that the owning chapter defines them, and glosses are given for mandates, recommerce, entitlements and the DSA transparency database.
results.corroborated_by: flowA A1 and flowB B2 (both report 'marketplace fitness functions' as unexplained)
